_method: preview_strategy_report, 1h anchor. Each transform is checked against its OWN trajectory slots in the same table, so no external data is needed and no sampling drift can creep in between the operand and the result. Where bars:'closed' was used, the trajectory slots were additionally diffed against data/audit/candles_btc_1h_battlegrid.json.
_why: docs/19 verified the METRICS (RSI, ATR, SMA, EMA) against the textbook. It did not touch the TRANSFORMS, which are the layer omega's whole column algebra sits on. Before this audit exactly one of the seventeen - spread - had ever been checked against its stated formula.

verified.stated: slots = last window non-null base values; trend = compare(first, last)
verified.check: CLOSE trajectory window=5 bars=closed on BTC returned 78740, 78924, 78971, 78729, 78996 - identical to the last five CLOSED candles (19:00 through 23:00 on 2026-08-24). Confirms both the slot semantics and that bars:'closed' really does exclude the forming bar.

verified.stated: |base[last] - base[first]| / sum(|base[i] - base[i-1]|) over the window
verified.check: BTC: |78996-78740| / (184+47+242+267) = 256/740 = 0.3459 -> rendered 0.35. SOL: a perfectly monotonic run, |99.05-96.50| / (0+0.99+0+1.56) = 2.55/2.55 = 1.000 -> rendered 1.00. The degenerate case landing exactly on 1.0 is the strong half of this.
BTC VOLUME window=4 bars=closed, using exact candle volumes: 1356.15 / (1315.32+1002.39+845.79+1356.15) = 0.30005 -> rendered 0.30. SOL: 448.4K / 894.9K = 0.5011 -> rendered 0.50.

First attempt used FUNDING_RATE, whose eight slots were all 0.0013 - a degenerate series that would match any central-tendency statistic, so it proved nothing. Re-run on OI window=6, which varies: SOL (441.3+443.6+443.6+458.7+492.2+519.1)/6 = 466.42 -> rendered $466.4M. DOGE 429.6/6 = 71.6 -> $71.6M. AVAX 95.5/6 = 15.92 -> $15.9M.
verified.result: exact on a varying series - it is the arithmetic mean, not a median

verified.check: Six columns across BTC and SOL, all consistent under interval arithmetic on the displayed operands. EMA5/EMA13 and rate/atrPct pin exactly; rate/chg24h only to 0.73pp because the denominator sits near zero. See docs/19.

verified.stated: ordinal(base among the ranked universe, by the chosen ordering)
verified.check: ATR_PCT ranked hi and lo across five coins. Ordering is monotone in the underlying value in both directions, and rank_hi + rank_lo = 79 = universe + 1 for EVERY coin (AVAX 36+43, BTC 48+31, DOGE 25+54, ETH 40+39, SOL 29+50). That identity holds only for a true tie-free ordinal over a fixed universe, and it holds five times out of five.
verified.result: exact - and proves hi/lo are exact inverses over 78 coins

verified.check: SMA20 value offset=3 rendered $78,215.50. Recomputing the 20-close mean from the cached candles, the window ending exactly 3 observations back gives 78215.50 - an exact match, and no neighbouring window comes close (2 back = 78275.85, 4 back = 78114.15). offset=0 was checked separately.

RSI14 value beside RSI14 classifyZone. BTC 57.1 -> neutral, DOGE 47.8 -> neutral, SOL 75.5 -> overbought. Consistent with the conventional 30/70 thresholds, and the emitted labels match the DECLARED vocabulary (overbought/oversold/neutral) - so the vocabulary defect recorded for ADX_zone and MFI14_zone is metric-specific, not universal.
verified.result: behaviourally exact on three coins; exact threshold not pinned from 3 points

verified.check: BB_PCT_B beside CLOSE bandTouch. BTC pctB 0.64 -> none, DOGE 0.43 -> none, SOL 1.20 -> upper. Direction confirmed: above the upper band reports 'upper'. The exact trigger threshold is not pinned - no observation sat between 0.64 and 1.20.
side=support returned 'bullish FVG' on all three coins, against a declared vocabulary of ['bullish FVG','bullish order block']. Support side yielding only bullish zone types is semantically correct.

STRUCT_ZONES count returned 16/15/17 on BTC/DOGE/SOL and 5-22 across commodities. Plausible cardinalities that vary sensibly by coin, but the underlying zone list is never exposed, so the count cannot be checked against it.

Scanned 30 coins for a live cross after the first attempt found none on three. MACD and ROC12 crossDetect beside their own 3-slot trajectories. Three fired - PUMP MACD Bearish, PUMP ROC Bearish, BTC ROC Bearish - and the decisive evidence is the ones that did NOT. GOOGL MACD ran -0.0065 -> +0.0275 -> +0.0660 and ZEC ran +0.4217 -> -0.2616 -> -0.7253: an unambiguous zero cross in each window, one bar earlier than the last pair, and crossDetect returned null on both. So it reads the LAST PAIR only, exactly as stated, and not 'a cross anywhere in the window'.
verified.caveat: The scope is proven. The exact trigger is not pinned to the digit: all three firing cases have operands that round to 0.00 at the displayed precision, so whether the test is a strict zero crossing or a sign change with a tolerance cannot be settled from the table.
verified.result: scope exact (last pair only); trigger threshold not pinned

verified.stated: output = [low, high] of nearest(base filtered by side)
verified.check: The rendered BTC support zone read $77,859.00-$77,923.00. Scanning 148 Hyperliquid 4h bars for bullish fair-value gaps - a 3-bar pattern where high[i-2] < low[i] - found exactly one at [77859, 77923], formed on the bar opening 2026-08-24T12:00Z. EXACT to the dollar on both bounds, and the next-closest of the 20 FVGs found is $2,594 away.
verified.result: exact - and it confirms nearestZoneType too: it really is a bullish FVG

verified.check: The FVG's third bar opens 08-24T12:00Z and closes 08-24T16:00Z. Rendered age was 21h with the current 1h bar at 13:00Z on 08-25. Counting from the bar's CLOSE gives exactly 21h; counting from its OPEN gives 25h. So detectedAt is the detecting bar's close, not its open.
verified.corrected: An earlier reading of 8h for the same zone was flagged as suspicious. It is consistent: 16:00Z + 8h = 08-25T00:00Z, so 13 hours of market time had genuinely passed between the two renders. The suspicion was unfounded and checking is what settled it.
verified.result: exact - hours since the DETECTING BAR CLOSED

verified.stated: output = ((price - midpoint) / midpoint) x 100  [WRONG - see BG-9]
verified.check: Measured as ((midpoint - price) / price) x 100 on three coins. This entry was previously filed under notVerified, which was a bookkeeping error on my part: the TRANSFORM was measured and works. What is wrong is the published formula, which is a documentation defect, not an unverified transform.
verified.result: exact - the published formula is what is wrong, not the engine

operationalFindings.finding: rank is scoped to the whole active market, not your coin selection
operationalFindings.evidence: The response carries rankScopingNote: 'Rank columns reflect the full active market, not the previewed coin selection - a coin may show a rank higher than the number of rows shown.' Ranks rendered as n/78 while only 5 coins were selected.
operationalFindings.consequence: Every cross-sectional family - carry-factor, xs-momentum, and the rest - ranks against 78 coins regardless of how many the strategy actually reads. A 'top decile' gate means top of 78, not top of your shortlist.

operationalFindings.finding: rank does NOT repaint intra-bar, unlike every other indicator
operationalFindings.evidence: Header meaning states: 'the standing as of the last close, unchanged until the next one.'
operationalFindings.consequence: A documented exception to cookbook trap 18. Rank columns are stable within the bar; value/trajectory/aggregate columns are not.

operationalFindings.evidence: In the same render, offset=0 drifted from the cached recomputation while offset=3 matched to the cent. An offset of 1 or more lands the window on closed bars, which no longer move.
operationalFindings.consequence: A second escape from cookbook trap 18, alongside bars:'closed' - and this one keeps the forming bar out of the window while still reading a metric that has no bars parameter of its own.

operationalFindings.finding: the rungs are fully modelled and omega predicts them exactly
operationalFindings.evidence: 21 columns spanning value, trajectory, distance, rank, spread, efficiency and classifyZone, rendered at rel:lower, rel:anchor and rel:regime simultaneously. All 30 headers matched omega.fanout's prediction, including the _ltf and _htf infixes and their interaction with trajectory slots (ADX_ltf_t2) and chained ranks (atrPct_htf_rank_hi). Values differ sensibly by rung - BTC RSI14 read 34.9 ltf, 48.8 anchor, 64.7 htf.
operationalFindings.consequence: The one hole flagged as genuinely unevidenced is closed. The 300-shape sweep ran at rel:anchor and never recorded the rung, so nothing in the repo showed lower/regime had been exercised systematically. They have now, and rung variants do not collide - the infix disambiguates the header, unlike offset (BG-8).

platformDefects.finding: Two columns whose headers collide RENDER, but both vanish from conditionColumns.
platformDefects.repro: One section, CLOSE trajectory window=6 bars=closed, SMA20 value offset=3, SMA20 value. The table renders 9 data columns and the header row reads '... | close_trend | SMA20 | SMA20 |' with two different values ($78,215.50 and $78,469.20). conditionColumns for that section lists SEVEN outputs - close_t5 through close_trend. NEITHER SMA20 appears.
platformDefects.why: offset is not part of the header name, so any two columns differing only by offset collide. The same applies to any other parameter the namer ignores.
platformDefects.cost: The agent still SEES both values as table text, so the table looks correct. But a condition referencing 'SMA20' has no column to bind to. Combined with BG-6 - a null read is FALSE, never UNRESOLVED - a gate written against that header fails silently and reads as a real negative.
platformDefects.control: SMA20 alone, without the offset twin, appears in conditionColumns normally with lt/lte/gte/gt/between. So the metric is conditionable; the COLLISION is what removes it.
platformDefects.suggestedFix: Either disambiguate the header when offset is set (SMA20_off3, as trajectory already does with _t3), or reject the section with REPORT_COLUMN_HEADER_COLLISION. Rendering a column that cannot be referenced is the worst of the three options.

platformDefects.finding: _authoring.json states nearestZoneDist = ((price - midpoint) / midpoint) x 100. The engine computes ((midpoint - price) / price) x 100 - the sign is INVERTED and the denominator is price, not the midpoint.
platformDefects.repro: STRUCT_ZONES nearestZoneDist side=support beside CLOSE and nearestZoneRange, on BTC/DOGE/SOL. BTC: support zone 77859-77923, midpoint 77891, close 78883. Stated formula gives +1.3%. Engine rendered -1.2%. All three coins render negative where the stated formula is positive. Solving ((mid - px)/px) for the price the engine used gives 78837 / 0.0902 / 100.46 against close columns of 78883 / 0.0905 / 100.57 - within 0.3%, consistent with the zone being read at the REGIME timeframe while close is the ANCHOR forming bar. The midpoint denominator is ruled out by SOL: it predicts -8.7% against a rendered -7.9%, while the price denominator predicts -8.0%.
platformDefects.cost: The header text - 'signed % from price to the nearest support zone midpoint' - matches the ENGINE. The machine-readable formula does not. Anyone building from the formula rather than the prose gets a gate with the sign reversed: 'price is above support' fires when price is below it.
platformDefects.suggestedFix: Correct the stated formula to ((midpoint - price) / price) x 100.

platformDefects.finding: For the SAME column, the section preamble and conditionColumns give contradictory descriptions of what a rung-scoped rank ranks against, and the preamble is wrong.
platformDefects.repro:
ATR_PCT rank ordering=hi at rel:lower, rel:anchor and rel:regime, with an EXPLICIT two-coin selection (BTC, SOL).
  preamble, atrPct_ltf_rank_hi: 'ordinal across THIS REPORT'S coins ... rendered as rank/report-size; computed per request, so it reflects the coins in this report and not the wider market'
  conditionColumns, same header: 'ordinal across the tracked universe ... rank/universe-size; the standing as of the last close, unchanged until the next one'
  rendered: BTC 47/78, SOL 20/78 - and the same for the _htf variants.
Report size is 2. Every denominator is 78. The values agree with conditionColumns and contradict the preamble. Only the anchor rung received preamble text that is correct for all three.
platformDefects.cost: The preamble is what an agent reads as table context. An author reading it would believe an _ltf or _htf rank gate is relative to their own shortlist and size a threshold accordingly - 'top 3' meaning top 3 of the coins they selected. It is actually top 3 of 78, so on a ten-coin selection that gate can match nothing at all.
platformDefects.suggestedFix: Make the preamble match conditionColumns and the values. If report-scoped ranking is the intended future behaviour for the rungs, it is not what ships today.

platformDefects.finding: ROC12 renders the raw fractional change while its column meaning says 'rate of change vs 12 bars ago (%)'. The value is 100x smaller than the label claims.
platformDefects.repro:
ROC12 at offset:1 beside a closed CLOSE trajectory of window 16, so the 12-bar and 15-bar references are both visible in the same table.
  HYPE  close_t12 79.76 -> close_now 79.91. 12-bar change = +0.00188 as a fraction, +0.19% as a percent. RENDERED: +0.00%. Only the fraction fits.
  ZEC   close_t12 836.45 -> 843.69 = +0.008656 fraction, +0.87% percent. RENDERED: +0.01%. Only the fraction fits.
  BTC   close_t12 79755 -> 78967 = -0.00988 fraction, -0.988% percent. RENDERED: -0.01%. Only the fraction fits.
HYPE also rules out the alternative that the lookback is 15 rather than 12: its 15-bar percent change is +2.50%, nothing like the rendered +0.00%.
platformDefects.cost: A threshold written from the label is wrong by 100x. 'ROC gt 2' meaning 'up 2 percent' has to be written 'ROC gt 0.02'. Because the value is small rather than absent, the gate does not error - it simply never fires, or always fires, depending on direction. The rel_roc_positive and rel_roc_negative scorecard signals read this metric.
platformDefects.note: PPO sits in the same module and the same table and IS a percent - measured -0.2477 against a rendered -0.25. So this is not a deliberate house convention applied consistently; ROC12 is the odd one out.
platformDefects.suggestedFix: Either multiply ROC12 by 100 to match its label, or change the label to drop the (%) and say it is a ratio. The first is almost certainly what was intended, given PPO's behaviour alongside it.
